name: Khronon-Screened Preferred-Frame with Independent Propagator
claimed_mechanism: The khronon defines a preferred frame and supplies the MOND interpolation through a screened preferred-frame coupling. A separate vector field carries the propagating degree of freedom with an independent kinetic normalization, so its finite propagation is not tied to the screened alpha response. The lapse-weighted coupling suppresses preferred-frame effects in high-acceleration regimes while leaving the propagator normalization intact.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field, low-acceleration limit the screened coupling approaches its unscreened value and reproduces the MOND acceleration law through the khronon preferred-frame sector. The vector propagator remains finite and unscreened, giving a well-defined propagation speed and kinetic normalization independent of the e^-y factor. In the high-acceleration regime the preferred-frame response is exponentially suppressed, recovering Newtonian behavior without damping the propagating mode.
inequivalence_argument: This is not a coefficient tweak of a killed architecture because it changes the field content and kinetic structure by adding an independent unscreened vector propagator alongside a screened khronon preferred-frame sector. The finite propagating-mode normalization is sourced independently rather than inherited from the screened coupling, which directly addresses the P7 collision. It is structurally distinct from nonlocal, degenerate-only, multi-sector, and constraint-first classes because the new architecture relies on a local screened preferred-frame coupling plus a separate local propagator.
